what: Builder told the user that Customer self-registration was open and listed test passwords without checking. The user said registration was not open.
why: Builder asserted login facts from a grep of seed scripts and a guess, without checking the realm or consulting the kb.
workaround: Created Keycloak user customer/customer through the admin REST API and tested a direct token login.

what: Builder said the catalog had no recipe for an actor without Keycloak. kb_search at L10185 returned the anonymous-actor section of accesspoint.md at rank 1, but the builder did not read it until the user said 'anonymous is the keyword'. GAPS item 8 repeated the wrong claim.
why: Builder did not kb_get the top hit before concluding the catalog was silent.
workaround: Read accesspoint.md 'Anonymous vs Authenticated Behaviour' at L10202 and built the anonymous actor from it.
gaps_ref: GAPS item 8 (earlier round, quoted at L10197)

what: Builder created an anonymous ActorType with managed=false, and the CLI rejected it: managed applies only when the actor is not anonymous.
why: Builder assumed managed applied to every actor; the CLI enforces the rule.
workaround: Dropped managed=false and created the actor with kind=HUMAN and anonymous=true.

what: A third actor makes the generated Admin dialogs import the same type twice (for example import type { ShopMessage, ShopMessage }), and biome format fails in webshop__admin. The builder's kb search for it found nothing, so it bisected the model by hand. The catalog already has a known-issue entry with the cause and the fix (create the new actor first, --index 0).
why: Generator (Zeta ESM to UI pass runs per actor in model file order; getApiImportsForPage uses a HashSet of ClassType). Builder never searched the kb for the duplicate-import error in this chunk.
workaround: Builder found the index-0 rule by bisection and applied it (Guest created with --index 0, build passed).
proposed_target: catalog/best-practices/frontend/dual-actor-frontend-architecture.md (link the known issue and the actor order rule)

what: Duplicate imports also appeared on main with no Guest actor, in ImportRunInfo.startImport dialogs, where undo shares its output type ShopMessage with startImport. Builder gave undo its own UndoMessage output and the build passed again. The catalog says a shared output with two actors alone did not reproduce the bug, so the cause is unproven.
why: Unknown; builder inferred a shared output type as the trigger from a single before and after result.
workaround: Changed ImportRunInfo.undo output to a new TO UndoMessage and updated UndoCustomImplementation.java.

what: After update ImportRunInfo.undo output=UndoMessage, validate passed but the Maven UI build failed with ActionContainerSameWithActionDefinition (the operation form action page container did not match). Running fill on the new TO fixed it.
why: The CLI changes the operation output without creating its UI pages; validate does not run the UI action check that the build runs.
workaround: Ran fill webshop::UndoMessage, then generate-root and generate, then rebuilt.

what: create -t TransferObjectType with -s mapping=webshop::Product auto-creates all mapped members ('+157 contained', then '+105 contained'). Builder then added DataMember rows by hand, and validation reported NamedElementIsUniqueInItsContainer and 'Binding ... is mapped by other mapped data members' errors.
why: CLI create of a TO with mapping already populates the members; a manual DataMember create duplicates them. The help text does not say so.
workaround: Deleted the TO with --cascade and re-created it, then added DataMembers with --no-check; final validate passed.

what: query -s cannot select a reference field: 'Subselection required for type ESM_Class of field target', and input{...} is 'not a field'. --where does not support fqn~ either.
why: CLI query takes only scalar fields; nested references need graphql.
workaround: Switched to judo graphql with nested items { } selections.
proposed_target: judo-cli query (-s nested references) or help text

what: GraphQL syntax is not in the help: a filter must be where:{name:{eq:"x"}} (where:{name:"x"} fails), and connection fields need items { } (name on ESM_DataFeatureConnection is undefined). The builder found each by trial error.
why: The graphql help shows no example of the where and connection shape.
workaround: Used where:{name:{eq:...}} and items { } in each query.
proposed_target: catalog graphql/CLI query reference (agent-docs/model) or CLI help

what: target/judo-cli.jar disappeared after generate or build runs, and every judo call failed with 'Unable to access jarfile'. Builder restored it with generate-root and later copied the jar to /tmp/judo-cli.jar.
why: Generation or build removes target/judo-cli.jar; cause not found.
workaround: Ran generate-root, then used /tmp/judo-cli.jar for later CLI calls.

what: After a new actor was added, generate did not add its module to frontend-react/pom.xml, e2e/pom.xml, karaf-features pom.xml and feature.xml; build -f did not pick it up. Builder copied those four files from the guest-actor branch.
why: Probable: module registration happens only in a full build or a generate-root step; not confirmed.
workaround: git checkout of the four files from branch guest-actor, then full build -i.

what: generate overwrote the new actor's hand-edited src/custom/application-customizer.tsx, and the builder had to rewrite it. Builder's GAPS note records this as item (c); text was cut in the transcript.
why: Custom file of the new actor was not listed in its .generator-ignore; generate replaces unlisted files.
workaround: Rewrote application-customizer.tsx after generate; regenerated later with the file in place.

what: Guessed REST path /api/webshop/Guest/products/~list returned 404. The working path is /api/webshop/Guest/Guest/products/~list (actor name repeated), found by reading the generated service file.
why: Builder guessed the path pattern without checking the catalog REST naming rule.
workaround: Read GuestServiceForProductsImpl.ts and used the path it contains.

what: kb_get agent-docs/frontend/extension-points.md with section 'Frontend Extension Points > Extra Routes > Dashboard Page' returned (not found). The kb_search parent heading was 'Extra Routes', but 'Dashboard Page' is a top-level section.
why: The heading path returned by kb_search as the parent does not match the section; kb_get needed the top-level heading.
workaround: Read the section from disk with grep (L10310).

what: kb_search 'root context redirect default application Karaf servlet / landing' returned only unrelated hits for the question of what the root URL serves and how to change it. Builder concluded there is no documented way.
why: No catalog section answers the root path question directly; the deployment Access Points entry (which says /apps/ lists bundles) was not in the top 5.
workaround: Used curl to check the root and /apps/ and reported no documented change path.
proposed_target: catalog/agent-docs/deployment/README.md (root path and how to set a default landing)

what: Builder read catalog files from disk instead of the kb: grep of 'supportGuestAccess' across the catalog, cat of role-landing-redirect-access-filter.md, and read of extension-points.md, although kb_search had returned the Guest Page section.
why: Builder bypassed kb after the read-discipline guard nudged it; no kb_get was made for those sections.
workaround: Used the disk text; the catalog content was correct.

what: The read-discipline guard fired more than 20 times ('Repeated source searching, still no kb consult'). Builder kept searching the generated source and the .scratch scripts with grep and ctx_search instead of kb_search for JUDO how-to questions.
why: Guard counts bash and ctx_search source lookups as source searching; many lookups were about generated code, which the kb does not index.
workaround: Builder kept going with grep and ctx_search; some lookups were answered by kb_search later.

what: Long foreground sleep (540 s) was aborted ('Command aborted'); the smoke run was never started and /tmp/smoke20.log does not exist. The user had to ask where it was running.
why: Builder put a 9 minute sleep in one bash call with a 600 s timeout; the run was started inside that call.
workaround: Reported the run as not started and offered to start it again in the background.

what: Builder used macOS-absent commands: setsid (not found) and timeout (not found). Both calls failed, and the builder had to retry with nohup.
why: Builder assumed GNU tools on macOS.
workaround: Retried with nohup and a plain background run.

what: Browser daemon failed to start ('Daemon process exited during startup'), so the Guest page check could not run for a few calls.
why: Stale agent-browser socket and pid files.
workaround: pkill agent-browser, removed the socket and pid files, and reopened the page.

what: User-reported Admin header problem (horizontal top bar with a scroll chevron and overflow menu) was not reproduced; the model has menuOrientation=VERTICAL for Admin. Left open, the builder asked which view the user sees.
why: Unclear: either a narrow-window layout or a different view than the builder checked.
workaround: None; asked the user for the screen and the desired layout.

what: Keycloak user customer/customer had to be created by hand through the admin REST API because there was no recipe for a first login user in the minimal app.
why: Known gap (GAPS item 8 from an earlier round); catalog recipe for seeding a first user not found in this chunk.
workaround: Created the user through the admin REST API and tested the token.

what: An actor with no principal and anonymous=true gets no realm or client, and its REST calls need no bearer token. Confirmed: /api/webshop/Guest/Guest/products/~list returned 200 with no token.
why: Platform behaviour as documented in accesspoint.md (Anonymous vs Authenticated Behaviour).

what: accesspoint.md marks access control for a call with no principal as 'Verify' (not checked). The builder did not check it either; it only confirmed that the call works with no token.
why: Catalog does not state whether an anonymous call can read more than the intended product fields.

what: supportGuestAccess is a property of the actor (ActorType), set with update <Actor> -s supportGuestAccess=true; update <Actor> --schema lists it, and it applies only when the actor is not anonymous. The catalog Guest Page entry states this.
why: Catalog extension-points.md Guest Page describes the flag and how to set it.

what: Put the Guest actor first in the model (create --index 0) so the generated Admin dialogs do not duplicate imports.
why: Avoid the Zeta per-actor order bug; catalog known-issue entry gives this workaround.
workaround: Guest created with --index 0; Admin build passed.

what: Interim public landing on Customer: set supportGuestAccess=true and register a GuestPage (Trail Shop title and Login / Register button), while the Guest actor was blocked.
why: Catalog Guest Page entry gives the documented way; user had asked for a public actor, so this is a stop-gap.

what: Admin home: register AdminHome as the DashboardPage visual element, which redirects / to the Dashboard view, instead of editing generated routes.
why: Catalog Dashboard Page entry: an empty dashboard renders the DashboardPage visual element; Customer already does the same with CatalogHome.

what: Give ImportRunInfo.undo its own output TO (UndoMessage) to clear the duplicate import, and change UndoCustomImplementation to return UndoMessage.
why: Builder read the shared output type as the trigger; catalog says a shared output alone did not reproduce it, so this is a workaround with an unproven cause.
workaround: Model change plus Java change; build -i passed; commit e4897a7.

what: Guest products access is read-only and derived: DERIVED getter webshop::Product!filter(p | p.active) on GuestProductInfo (name, sku, price, unit, description).
why: Show only active products to the public; keep the public TO minimal.

what: Public Guest actor (anonymous, HUMAN, first in model) with read-only GuestProductInfo TO and products access; products page at /webshop/Guest/ with no login.
Guest home redirect (GuestHome) to the product list and GuestBar Login / Register button linking to /webshop/Customer/; Guest branding (title, logo, colours, horizontal menu) and menu label Products.
Admin home: AdminHome component and registerAdminHome hook redirect / to the Dashboard view (DashboardPage visual element).
Customer guest page: registerGuestPage hook with Trail Shop title and Login / Register button, and supportGuestAccess=true on Customer.
ImportRunInfo.undo returns its own UndoMessage TO (model plus UndoCustomImplementation.java), which clears the admin duplicate-import error.
Customer shop logo hook (registerShopLogoHook) copied to the Guest app, and trail-shop icon and logo assets copied to its public folder.
